To find the eigenvalues of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), we first need to set up the characteristic polynomial by calculating the determinant of \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 - \lambda & 2 \\ 2 & 2 - \lambda \end{bmatrix}\). 

The determinant is given by:

\[
(5 - \lambda)(2 - \lambda) - (2)(2)
\]

Expanding this, we have:

\[
(5 - \lambda)(2 - \lambda) - 4 = 10 - 5\lambda - 2\lambda + \lambda^2 - 4
\]

This simplifies to:

\[
\lambda^2 - 7\lambda + 6
\]

To find the eigenvalues, we solve the equation:

\[
\lambda^2 - 7\lambda + 6 = 0
\]

Factoring this polynomial:

\[
(\lambda - 1)(\lambda - 6) = 0
\]

So, the eigenvalues are:

\[
\lambda = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad \lambda = 6
\]

Final answer: 1, 6
